tax_notes.WA: Two local lodging taxes feed the city or county lodging tax fund that the LTAC allocates. (1) Basic tax up to 2% (RCW 67.28.180) is credited against the 6.5% state sales tax, so it costs the guest nothing extra. Cities in King County other than Bellevue, and Yakima County cities other than Yakima, cannot levy it. (2) Additional tax up to 2% (RCW 67.28.181) is added on top of sales tax. Several jurisdictions are exempt or grandfathered at other rates (e.g., Pierce, Snohomish, Grays Harbor and Cowlitz counties and their cities, plus Bellevue, Yakima, Wenatchee, East Wenatchee). Both must be spent on tourism promotion or tourism-related facilities. Typical total is 4%. Where both are levied, about 4% of the room rate lands in the LTAC fund ($6 on a $150 night). These do not flow to LTAC: the Washington State Convention Center PFD tax (7% in Seattle, 2.8% in the rest of King County, RCW 36.100.040, paid to the PFD), tourism promotion area (TPA) fees (a separate assessment), sales tax, and other PFD taxes. Calculator rule: grant-fund return = room revenue x the jurisdiction's combined 67.28.180 + 67.28.181 rate (usually 4%).
tax_notes.OR: Each city or county sets its own local transient lodging tax (TLT) rate, and that revenue stays local. ORS 320.350 grandfathers how pre-July 2003 taxes are used. For new or increased local TLT since 2003, at least 70% must go to tourism promotion or tourism-related facilities, and up to 30% may go to general use. HB 4148 (2026) lets a local government choose to move that split to 50/50 starting Jan 1, 2027. It is optional, not automatic. The state TLT is 1.5% for stays through Dec 31, 2026. It goes to the state, not to the local fund: Travel Oregon, which sends 20% to the seven regional tourism organizations and also runs statewide competitive grants. HB 4134 raises the state rate to 2.75% for nights beginning on or after Jan 1, 2027. The extra 1.25 points is billed as a 'nature conservation fee' and funds wildlife and conservation programs, not tourism. Calculator rule: local tourism-fund return = room revenue x local TLT rate x 70% (or 50% if the jurisdiction adopts the HB 4148 option, or the grandfathered share for pre-2003 taxes). The state 1.5%/2.75% is excluded.
tax_notes.ID: Idaho has no general city or county lodging tax. Only resort cities (local-option tax set by voters) and auditorium districts (e.g., Greater Boise Auditorium District) levy local room taxes. That money stays local. Auditorium district money is generally spent on the district's convention or event facility, not open grants. The statewide 2% travel and convention tax on hotels, motels, vacation rentals and private campgrounds is split 45% back to the region it was collected in, as Idaho Regional Travel and Convention (ITC) grants to nonprofit regional travel organizations, 45% to statewide promotion, and 10% to program administration. Calculator rule: regional ITC grant return = room revenue x 2% x 45% = 0.9% of room revenue, plus the local resort-city or auditorium-district rate where one applies (the rate varies by jurisdiction).
